column4: Dialect-arm SUBTEST population, one line for the whole shape rather than one per test: this job runs the full unfiltered ./engine/... ./migration/... sweep with ONLY CLEAT_TEST_MYSQL set, so every test with a per-dialect t.Run("postgres", ...) skips that arm here. Measured on a real CI run (cleat#2444, PR #2686, run 36617238081, job 109573287782): `grep '"Action":"skip"' test-report.json | grep -o '"Test":"[^"]*"' | grep -c '/postgres$'` = 405. Bumped to 406 for cleat#2228's TestCleanupTestDataClearsTenantScopedFixtureTables/postgres, which matches this bare suffix pattern too -- check-skip-budget.sh checks each line independently, so a new test's arm counts against BOTH its own named line and any broader suffix line it also matches; the checker cannot distinguish that from something genuinely undeclared. Filed as cleat#2729; this is the workaround, not the fix, and it edits a count this design was meant to keep out of any one PR's way. Bumped to 407 for cleat#1986's TestWorkflowDefDefaultsToTheAuthExposureClass/postgres, same reason. Bumped to 408 for cleat#1984's TestResolveAmbiguity_NotSentRecordsARetryableFailure/postgres, landing in the same rebase as #1986 -- measured: CI run 36865282850 (Test MySQL, job 110379530838) at d51e679b, check-skip-budget.sh's per-line check (every ledger line checked individually, `got -ne count` fails loudly) passed exact. A second independent bump landed on develop after this PR's own re-measurement: cleat#2891's own new test bumped this same broad line by +1 again (407 -> 408), on top of cleat#1986's earlier +1 (406 -> 407). So the full stack is base 406 + 1 (#1986) + 1 (#2891) + 2 (cleat#1980, this PR) = 410. Not re-measured fresh against this exact combination; the mechanism (each new dialect-parameterised test independently adding its own skip to the same broad suffix line) is the same one already tool-verified once on this line, so the arithmetic is trusted here rather than re-run, given how quickly this line moves under concurrent work. Measured on run 36799321585, job 110169881893 (develop HEAD 3f08fd89, 2026-10-01): replicated check-skip-budget.sh's own attribution algorithm exactly (specific named lines removed from the skip-name pool first, then broad suffix lines, most-specific-first, matching the script's own pool-reduction order) rather than a plain name count, since several of this job's skips are already claimed by their own dedicated ledger lines elsewhere (e.g. test-areclaimwindowpast24daysdoesnotoverflow, the-mssql-snapshot-sees-the-attributes-it-selects.tsv) and a naive total-minus-two-suffixes count overlapped them: 333 names matched neither /postgres$ nor /mssql$ directly, but 9 of those are already named elsewhere, leaving exactly 324 -- matching this line's inherited budget exactly, with zero mismatches on every other ledger line for this job (specific or broad) against the same run. May only shrink: as a remaining name here gets dialect-parameterised and its own named line, delete it from this alternation and lower the count by one.

test-plugin-migrations' unfiltered ./plugins/... step, all three DSNs set -- the step cleat#2444 is about. Measured on the same CI run (job 109573287579): self-explanatory in its own -v output and not dialect-invisible: "MySQL is single-tenant by constraint (engine.DefaultTenantUUID, all zeros) -- an uppercase tenant id cannot be constructed here, and this dialect was never where the case bug lived". This line originally also covered TestNextRun_Feb29NonLeapYear (count 2, an alternation), but cleat#2839/#2851 replaced that test with two that assert instead of skip -- check-skip-budget.sh's own equality check (`got != count` fails either direction) means a line still expecting 2 would go from "correctly grants a skip" to "grants a skip that no longer exists" the moment #2851 merges, so the count and pattern are narrowed here rather than left to redden the next PR's Plugin Migrations step for a change nobody made.

Both CLEAT_CRASH_MYSQL and CLEAT_CRASH_MSSQL are set here, so the four subtests TestShutdownScenariosOnMySQLAndMSSQL selects should not skip at all. Measured on the same CI run (job 109573287949): the step passed with 0 skips, confirming the prediction. Not a placeholder -- this is the real value.
